- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by 2–5% relative to recent mean.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; apply lag correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast for days 1–5.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model overshoots by 5–10% in next 5–7 days; apply dampening factor to forecast tail.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >90% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 10–15%.
- Sentiment history with 0.00s dominates; model shows persistent underestimation; add 3–5% bias to forecast for low-sentiment periods.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in first 10 days of 30-day horizon; apply early correction: subtract 2–4% from first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
